title: Adani Ports incorporates Oman subsidiary as it is linked to Salalah concession succession
summary: APSEZ incorporated Indian Ocean Gateway Terminal in Oman on 21 October 2026 via Adani International Ports Holdings, days after Oman's transport ministry confirmed it will not extend the Salalah Port Services concession (APM Terminals-managed) expiring 1 November 2028. Industry sources report APSEZ is in advanced talks to take over Salalah (4.3m TEU in 2025, 6m TEU capacity, Gemini hub). Would give Adani a second Arabian Sea transshipment hub competing directly with DP World's Jebel Ali and Sokhna network.

title: Adani Ports Q2 FY27: cargo up 15% to 142 MMT, profit up 16.5%, guidance raised
summary: For the quarter ended 30 September 2026 APSEZ handled 142 MMT (+15% YoY), posted consolidated net profit of INR 36.2bn (+16.5%) and revenue of INR 113.4bn (+23.7%). August set a monthly record of 50 MMT. FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR 440-460bn; capex guidance raised to INR 150-170bn. Four international facilities handled 24 MMT with revenue up 71% YoY.

title: Adani Ports wins 30-year BOT concession for two dry bulk berths at Paradip Port
summary: Paradip Port Authority issued a Letter of Award to APSEZ to develop and operate two mechanised dry bulk berths on a 30-year build-operate-transfer basis, adding 18 MMT of capacity. This takes APSEZ's Indian capacity to 671 MMT across 16 ports/terminals and deepens its east-coast footprint.

title: Gujarat Maritime Board signals concession extensions for Adani's Mundra and Pipavav
summary: Gujarat Maritime Board sent Letters of Comfort indicating intent to extend concessions at Mundra and Pipavav, subject to investment plans. Extension clears the way for Adani to lift Mundra container capacity by over 50% within five years (c.100 MMT addition per Investec); Dahej and Hazira concessions (expiring 2031-35) expected to follow. Removes a key overhang on APSEZ's flagship 274 MMT Mundra hub.

title: MSC to take 49% of Adani's Vizhinjam port; Adani targets concession to 2080
summary: Adani Vizhinjam Ports plans to bring in MSC as a 49% equity partner to fund the INR 16,000 crore final phase, with MSC positioning Vizhinjam as a main transshipment hub. Completing the final phase by December 2028 would make Adani eligible for a 20-year extension taking the concession to 2080 (currently 2060 after the Nov 2024 supplementary agreement). Stake transfer requires Kerala and CCI approval.

title: Adani Harbour International acquires 51% of Argentina's Meridian Transportes Marítimos
summary: Adani Harbour International FZCO (APSEZ step-down subsidiary) signed an SPA on 15 May 2026 to buy 51% of Meridian Transportes Marítimos SA from Logistica y Servicios Maritimos and Simpo, creating a nautical-services JV. Key asset is Meridian's 10-year contract with Southern Energy SA (signed Dec 2025) to supply six vessels. First Adani marine-services footprint in South America; value undisclosed.

title: Adani Ports FY26: cargo crosses 500 MMT, revenue up 25%, logistics revenue up 55%
summary: APSEZ handled 500.8 MMT in FY26 (+11%), with revenue INR 38,736 crore (+25%), EBITDA INR 22,851 crore (+20%) and PAT INR 12,782 crore (+16%). International ports revenue rose 34% to INR 4,539 crore with EBITDA margin up to 28.6%; logistics revenue rose 55% to INR 4,478 crore and rail volumes 8% to 695,517 TEU.

title: Adani Ports completes 100% acquisition of North Queensland Export Terminal (Abbot Point)
summary: APSEZ closed its all-stock acquisition of NQXT, a 50 MTPA multi-user coal export terminal at Abbot Point, from promoter entities Carmichael Rail and Port Singapore Holdings, after RBI, FIRB and minority-shareholder approvals. Deal announced April 2025 at an enterprise value of c.USD 2.4bn; lease runs to 2110. First Australian terminal for APSEZ and step toward its 1bn-tonne-by-2030 target.
partners: Carmichael Rail and Port Singapore Holdings

title: Adani-led Colombo West International Terminal starts operations
summary: The USD 800m Colombo West International Terminal (CWIT), developed by APSEZ with John Keells Holdings and Sri Lanka Ports Authority under a 35-year BOT, began operations on 7 April 2025. The 1,400m-quay, 20m-draft terminal is Colombo's first fully automated deep-water facility with c.3.2m TEU/yr capacity, strengthening Adani's transshipment play against regional hubs.

title: Adani Ports buys 80% of OSV operator Astro Offshore for USD 185m
summary: APSEZ agreed to acquire 80% of Astro Offshore, a Dubai-headquartered operator of 26 offshore support vessels (AHTs, barges, MPSVs) active in the Middle East, India, Far East and Africa, for USD 185m cash (EV USD 235m, 4.4x FY25E EBITDA). Takes Adani's marine fleet to 168 vessels and signals its ambition to become one of the world's largest marine operators, competing with DP World's P&O Maritime.

title: Adani secures in-principle approval for USD 1.9bn Lien Chieu greenfield port in Da Nang
summary: Karan Adani said APSEZ received in-principle approval from the Vietnamese government to develop the wharf area of Lien Chieu Port, Da Nang, estimated at USD 1.9bn, with public funds of c.USD 140m for breakwaters, channel and access roads. Master plan foresees eight container and six general cargo berths; phase one two 750m berths for 8,000+ TEU ships. First Adani port project in Southeast Asia.

title: Adani Ports signs 30-year concession for Container Terminal 2 at Dar es Salaam
summary: APSEZ signed a 30-year agreement with Tanzania Ports Authority to operate and manage Dar es Salaam's Container Terminal 2 (four berths, c.1m TEU/yr, 820,000 TEU handled in 2023). In parallel its East Africa Gateway JV with AD Ports Group and East Harbour Terminals bought 95% of Tanzania International Container Terminal Services from Hutchison for USD 39.5m. Adani's first African port, in a market where DP World already runs Dar es Salaam berths 0-7 under its 2023 concession.

title: Yilport commits EUR 100m to expand Leixões North Container Terminal to 1m TEU
summary: At Porto Maritime Week Yilport unveiled a EUR 100m plan to expand and modernise Leixões' North Container Terminal, roughly quintupling its capacity to c.1m TEU/yr, accommodating 300m vessels and adding a rail terminal. Ten automated Konecranes E-Hybrid RTGs from the July 2026 order are earmarked for the site, which was operating at 88% capacity.

title: Yilport announces EUR 891m Turkish port investment plan under new owner CoreX Holding
summary: Following the split of the Yildirim family group, Yilport now sits under Amsterdam-based CoreX Holding BV, founded by Robert Yüksel Yildirim. On 17 September 2026 the operator announced a EUR 891m (c.USD 1bn) investment programme for its Turkish ports, complementing environmental filings for capacity expansion (reclamation, quays, dredging) at Dilovası/Gebze filed in April 2026.

title: Taranto port authority moves to call in Yilport's EUR 3m guarantee over missed traffic targets
summary: The Ionian Sea Port System Authority sought to cash a EUR 3.05m guarantee from San Cataldo Container Terminal (Yilport's Italian subsidiary), alleging breach of its 49-year Taranto concession through years of missed container volume targets. Yilport responded on 24 September 2026 that it remains committed but that unfinished dredging restricts the terminal. Dispute flags execution risk on Yilport's Mediterranean hub ambitions.
partners: Port System Authority of the Ionian Sea

title: Yilport Gävle container volumes up 16% in H1 2026 on MENA flows and forest products
summary: Yilport's Gävle terminal, Sweden's largest container port, handled 16% more containers in H1 2026 than a year earlier, driven by existing customers, forest products and new flows to and from the Middle East and North Africa. In the same month Yilport Gebze (Turkey) reported a 21% yard productivity gain from RTG optimisation.

title: Yilport orders 53 Konecranes E-Hybrid RTGs for Portugal, El Salvador and Ghana
summary: Yilport placed a 53-unit E-Hybrid RTG order with Konecranes (booked Q2 2026): 10 automated units each for Liscont (Lisbon) and Leixões, 18 for UPdP Acajutla in El Salvador and 15 for ATSL-Takoradi in Ghana, delivered in batches over 16-22 months. One of the largest single RTG orders of 2026, underpinning Yilport's multi-continent capacity programme.

title: Yilport shortlisted for Chornomorsk container terminals concession in Ukraine
summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Development admitted four bidders to competitive dialogue for the concession of Chornomorsk's First Container Terminal and Container Terminal: APM Terminals, Yilport Holding, a Mariner/TAS consortium and an AD Ports Group/SKF Holdings consortium. Billed as potentially the largest investment in Ukrainian port history (hundreds of millions of dollars). DP World is not among the finalists.

title: Yilport adds two mobile harbour cranes at Takoradi as throughput doubles
summary: Yilport ATSL-Takoradi (Ghana's western corridor) commissioned two additional mobile harbour cranes, taking its fleet to five, after throughput doubled since operations began in September 2024. Six STS cranes and RTGs are under tender and 15 electric RTGs have been ordered from Konecranes, signalling a move toward a fully equipped container terminal competing with Tema (Meridian Port Services) for Ghana and Sahel cargo.

title: Yilport and Altıntel file for capacity expansion at Dilovası (Kocaeli)
summary: Yilport Holding and Altıntel Liman filed environmental applications for port capacity expansion at Dilovası east of Istanbul, covering reclamation, quay construction and dredging to raise vessel and cargo handling capacity at Yilport's home-market Gebze/Dilovası cluster.

title: Yilport handles 8.4m TEU in 2025, up 12%; Puerto Bolívar +63%
summary: Yilport group container volumes rose 12% to 8.4m TEU in 2025 (7.5m in 2024), with general cargo +10%. Puerto Bolívar (Ecuador) grew 63%, El Salvador terminals 14%, Liscont 14%, Gävle 12%, Oslo 11%, Turkish terminals 12%; Takoradi roughly doubled; Iberian intermodal volumes rose c.400%. Confirms Yilport's position as a fast-growing mid-tier global operator.

title: Ferrol port authority extends Yilport's container terminal concession by 15 years to 2063
summary: The Ferrol-San Cibrao Port Authority approved a substantial modification of the Ferrol Container Terminal concession requested by Yilport Holding, extending it 15 years to September 2063. Comes after a year in which the terminal's future was uncertain and as Ferrol doubled transshipment volumes in 2025.

title: Yilport's UPdP takes over operations at Acajutla and La Unión, El Salvador
summary: Unión Portuaria del Pacífico (80% Yilport, 20% state agency CEPA) began operating the Acajutla and La Unión terminals on 16 December 2024 under a 50-year concession extendable by 50 years. Marks Yilport's second Central American operation after Puerto Quetzal; volumes rose 14% in 2025 and 18 E-Hybrid RTGs were ordered in 2026.

title: Yilport wins 50-year concession for El Salvador's Acajutla and La Unión ports with USD 1.6bn commitment
summary: President Bukele announced a 50-year concession to Yilport to modernise Acajutla (tripling terminal capacity) and activate the underused La Unión port (dredging, new cranes) with investment of c.USD 1.615bn, the largest private investment in the country's history. Structured through a mixed-economy company with state agency CEPA.

title: Yilport inaugurates Berth 6 and 1m TEU yard at Puerto Bolívar, Ecuador
summary: Yilport inaugurated Container Berth 6 (450m extension) and a new container yard at Puerto Bolívar, with equipment supporting 1m TEU/yr and channel deepened to 14.5m (16.5m targeted 2025). Phase one represents over USD 400m of the USD 750m+ committed under the 50-year concession. Terminal volumes grew 63% in 2025.

title: Yilport Oslo orders three Kalmar electric reachstackers and renews maintenance contract
summary: Yilport Oslo Terminal ordered three Kalmar electric reachstackers in March 2026, following a January 2026 renewal of its Kalmar maintenance contract, as part of Yilport's fleet electrification across Nordic terminals. Oslo volumes grew 11% in 2025.

title: GT Lines launches Khorfakkan-Berbera Express feeder to Somaliland
summary: Gulftainer's shipping arm GT Lines announced the Khorfakkan Berbera Express (KBX), a direct fortnightly container service between Khorfakkan and Berbera starting November 2026, connected to GT Lines' wider feeder network. Puts Gulftainer in direct competition with DP World's Berbera terminal hinterland feedering and its Jebel Ali-Berbera links.

title: GT Lines starts Khorfakkan-Djibouti shuttle (Khorfakkan Red Sea Express)
summary: GT Lines launched KRX 1, a fortnightly single-vessel shuttle Khorfakkan-Djibouti-Khorfakkan in October 2026, giving Gulf-of-Oman cargo access to Djibouti and the Ethiopian hinterland while bypassing Hormuz. First of the East Africa/Red Sea services Gulftainer promised under its USD 2bn strategy.

title: Gulftainer wins EGA aluminium export routing through Khorfakkan (up to 300,000 t/yr)
summary: Emirates Global Aluminium agreed to route east-coast aluminium exports through Khorfakkan Port, with Gulftainer building out dedicated port capabilities. Volumes of up to 250,000 tonnes in year one and 300,000 tonnes in year two, with further growth possible, diversifying EGA away from Hormuz-exposed gateways such as Jebel Ali.

title: Khorfakkan capacity reaching 5m TEU by end-October 2026 as Hormuz disruption drives 700% volume jump
summary: Gulftainer's USD 2bn Khorfakkan expansion is on track to lift capacity from 3.5m to 5m TEU by end-October 2026 (c.100k TEU/week), after weekly throughput surged from c.8k to 65k TEU following the Iran conflict and Hormuz war-risk rerouting. Phases 2-3 target 10m+ TEU within three years; truck gate capacity up to 12,000/day; GT Lines fleet grown to 15 vessels. Gulftainer estimated it handled 80-90% of UAE container demand at the peak of disruption.
partners: Sharjah Ports, Customs and Free Zones Authority

title: Gulftainer enters Thailand with strategic investment in Suksawat Terminal near Bangkok
summary: Gulftainer signed a binding agreement for a strategic investment in Suksawat Terminal on the Chao Phraya River (Samut Prakan), which serves Greater Bangkok with barge links to Laem Chabang. Stake and value undisclosed; Gulftainer plans to invest in capacity and productivity and build inland logistics and industrial infrastructure around it. First Southeast Asian asset and first new overseas terminal since Wilmington/Canaveral.

title: Gulftainer launches Sajaa Bonded Dry Port linked to Khorfakkan
summary: Gulftainer launched a bonded corridor from Khorfakkan Port to its Sajaa inland facility in Sharjah (c.90 km), with rates effective 1 August 2026. Handles dry, reefer, DG and empty containers, offers 12 days free storage and claims up to 20% logistics cost savings, positioned to serve c.70% of the UAE market. Part of 2.3m TEU of planned inland capacity with Al Dhaid.

title: Gulftainer unveils USD 2bn 'global trade infrastructure' strategy centred on Khorfakkan
summary: Gulftainer announced a USD 2bn strategy shifting from terminal operator to integrated platform across four units (GT Ports, GT Logistics, GT Parks, GT Maritime/GT Lines), positioning Sharjah within IMEC and Belt and Road. Includes Khorfakkan expansion from 3.5m to 5m TEU (10m+ long term), 2.3m TEU of inland capacity at Al Dhaid and Sajaa, an Etihad Rail connection agreement, and a 10-vessel chartered GT Maritime fleet linking Asia and South Asia to the UAE.

title: Gulftainer's GT Lines launches dedicated UAE-Umm Qasr feeder service
summary: GT Lines began its first dedicated feeder linking UAE gateways with Umm Qasr, using own vessels and integrated with Gulftainer's Iraq Commercial Terminal and Umm Qasr Logistics Centre (warehousing, storage, consolidation, customs). GT Lines fleet stood at 10 vessels covering the Gulf, Iraq, India, Pakistan, China and SE Asia. Competes with Unifeeder/DP World on the Iraq corridor.

title: Gulftainer announces 150-hectare Al Dhaid Multi-Modal Logistics Hub and Freezone (1.5m TEU)
summary: Gulftainer unveiled the Al Dhaid Multi-Modal Trade Corridor, a 150-ha inland hub c.50-60 km from Khorfakkan with 1.5m TEU/yr capacity, container yard and empty depot, CFS with same-day port shuttles, warehousing and cold storage, and Etihad Rail intermodal access to Saudi Arabia and Oman. Developed as a PPP with Sharjah Ports, Customs and Free Zones Authority; investment and timeline undisclosed. Direct inland competitor to Jafza/National Industries Park model.
partners: Sharjah Ports, Customs and Free Zones Authority

title: Gulftainer launches India-Gulf Express (GIX) weekly service
summary: Gulftainer launched GIX, a weekly direct service linking Nhava Sheva and Mundra with Sharjah (Khorfakkan), Sohar, Hamad and Jebel Ali, leveraging its terminals, bonded hubs and trucking fleet to cut lead times. Marked Gulftainer's move into liner-type shipping ahead of the 2026 GT Lines build-out.

title: Gulftainer launches 50-hectare K-Flow integrated logistics facility at Khorfakkan
summary: Gulftainer launched K-Flow, a scalable 50-ha integrated logistics facility at Khorfakkan Commercial Terminal developed with Khorfakkan Customs, offering warehousing, cold chain, distribution and CFS operations designed to cut handoffs, dwell time and landed cost. Precursor to the Sajaa and Al Dhaid inland network.

title: Gulftainer's GSCCO handles first ship-to-rail import containers at Jubail for Riyadh
summary: Gulf Stevedoring Contracting Company, Gulftainer's Saudi subsidiary, stevedored MSC Danit at Jubail Container Terminal and moved 59 import containers onto a Saudi Arabia Railways train to Riyadh within 24 hours, in a ceremony attended by Mawani, SAR, MSC and Saudi Customs. Demonstrates Gulftainer's rail-linked inland offering in the Eastern Province.

title: Gulftainer expands Umm Qasr Logistics Centre from 50,000 to 350,000 sqm
summary: Gulftainer's Momentum Logistics is expanding the Umm Qasr Logistics Centre adjacent to Iraq Commercial Terminal from 50,000 sqm to 350,000 sqm, with road transit solutions planned towards Jordan, and provided logistics support for Iraq Ministry of Electricity equipment shipments. Gulftainer has operated in Iraq since 2010.

title: Bangladesh directs port authority to appoint RSGT as operator of Chattogram Container Terminal
summary: Bangladesh's Ministry of Shipping (letter dated 28 September 2026) instructed Chittagong Port Authority to begin appointing Red Sea Gateway Terminal as operator of the Chattogram Container Terminal (CCT), whose Saif Powertec contract expires 2 November 2026. Would make RSGT operator of two Chittagong terminals alongside Patenga, while DP World holds the separate 15-year New Mooring concession signed 8 October 2026. Terms not yet disclosed; local opposition reported.

title: RSGT inaugurates USD 170m Patenga Container Terminal, doubling capacity to 500,000 TEU
summary: Red Sea Gateway Terminal International formally inaugurated its USD 170m Patenga Container Terminal at Chittagong, Bangladesh's first international port concession (22 years, awarded 2023). Four new STS cranes doubled capacity from 250,000 to 500,000 TEU and RSGT claims 30% higher productivity than regional peers. RSGT holds 36.36% via Red Sea Port Development Co. (SISCO group) and signalled up to USD 1bn further investment in Bangladesh's maritime sector.

title: RSGT's Patenga terminal handles 154,564 TEU and 78 vessels in 2025
summary: In its first full calendar year under RSGT management (operations began June 2024), Patenga Container Terminal handled 78 vessels and 154,564 TEU, ramping toward its 500,000 TEU capacity. Performance underpins the Bangladeshi government's move to hand RSGT the adjacent CCT.

title: RSGT Bangladesh begins operating Patenga Container Terminal under 22-year concession
summary: RSGT Bangladesh started operations at Chittagong's Patenga Container Terminal in June 2024 under a 22-year concession with Chittagong Port Authority, RSGT's first terminal outside Saudi Arabia. Established the Saudi operator as a competitor to DP World in the Bay of Bengal ahead of DP World's own New Mooring award in 2026.

title: Tanger Med 3: APM Terminals signs concession for 4.5m TEU terminal; complex to reach 20m TEU
summary: At a royal working session on 28 October 2026 Morocco signed a concession with Maersk/APM Terminals for a new 1,200m-quay, 4.5m TEU/yr container terminal at Tanger Med 3, west of Tanger Med 2, with private investment of MAD 8bn. Overall Tanger Med 3 programme exceeds EUR 2.1bn (EUR 1.4bn+ private, EUR 730m public); operations due mid-2031. Would lift the Tanger Med complex toward 20m TEU, cementing its lead as Africa's and the Mediterranean's largest container port.

title: Tanger Med H1 2026 traffic reaches 84m tonnes (+6%), revenue +8.6%
summary: Tanger Med Port Authority reported 84 million tonnes of cargo in H1 2026, including 45 million tonnes in Q2, with cargo up 6% and revenue up 8.6%, driven by new maritime links, Gemini hub status and logistics zone activity, in a half-year marked by Hormuz/Red Sea rerouting toward the western Mediterranean.

title: Tanger Med tenders enabling works for western port expansion
summary: Tanger Med Port Authority issued tender TMPA_AO_40_26 for enabling infrastructure works (diversion and extension of drainage culverts at Tanger Med 2 and the western platform) tied to the planned western expansion of the complex, following a broader expansion tender launched in December 2025 and the authority's March 2026 statement that it is adding capacity in response to the Gulf war.

title: Tanger Med Port Authority receives first investment-grade ratings (S&P BBB-, Moody's Baa3)
summary: TMPA was assigned first-time long-term ratings of BBB- (stable) by S&P and Baa3 (stable) by Moody's, at sovereign level, as it prepares to substantially increase borrowing to fund Tanger Med 3 and the western expansion. Ratings cite its role as Gemini Cooperation hub and Africa's largest container port.

title: Tanger Med Port Authority to take 44% of Morocco's single-window operator Portnet
summary: TMPA will acquire a 44.07% stake in state-owned Portnet SA, operator of Morocco's national single window for foreign trade formalities, through a capital increase. Gives Tanger Med control over a key trade-digitalisation platform used by all Moroccan ports, reinforcing its port-community-system leadership (ranked a digital 'technology pioneer' and 16th globally for containers in July 2026).

title: Hapag-Lloyd's Hanseatic Global Terminals doubles its stake in Tanger Med terminal
summary: Alongside acquiring 20% of Eurogate's Hamburg terminal, Hapag-Lloyd's terminal arm Hanseatic Global Terminals agreed to double its shareholding in its Tanger Med container terminal, deepening carrier commitment to Tanger Med as the Gemini Cooperation's West Mediterranean hub and shifting volumes away from Algeciras (confirmed by the US FMC in October 2026 for Maersk's US-flag calls).

title: Tanger Med industrial platform generates MAD 188bn (EUR 17.3bn) in 2025, up 8%
summary: Tanger Med Group reported that the industrial cluster around the port (Tanger Free Zone, Tanger Automotive City, Tétouan and other zones) generated MAD 188bn / EUR 17.3bn of revenue in 2025, up 8%, led by the automotive sector. New plant openings continued in 2026 (e.g. SFC Solutions Group, May 2026). Benchmark for DP World's Jafza and Africa zones.

title: Tanger Med expands cargo capacity to absorb Gulf-war rerouting
summary: Tanger Med announced it is increasing cargo-handling capacity to prevent congestion as the US/Israel-Iran war pushed more shipping away from Bab el-Mandeb and Suez toward Atlantic and western Mediterranean routings; Moroccan transshipment rose 28.6% in H1 2026. Operational response ahead of structural Tanger Med 3 capacity.

title: Tanger Med handles record 11.1m TEU and c.161m tonnes in 2025
summary: Tanger Med port complex handled 11,106,164 TEU in 2025, up 8.4% from 10.24m, and total cargo of c.161 million tonnes, aided by the latest expansion phase at APM Terminals' TC4 (two new ZPMC STS cranes delivered December 2025) and rising liquid bulk. TMPA revenue reached MAD 4.43bn, up 10.3%. Ranked 16th globally for container traffic.

title: Tanger Med launches tender for further port expansion
summary: Tanger Med Port Authority launched a tender in December 2025 for the next phase of expansion of the port complex, preceding the August 2026 enabling-works tender and the October 2026 Tanger Med 3 concession signing with APM Terminals.

title: Tanger Med T4 (APM Terminals MedPort) adds two ZPMC STS cranes
summary: Two new ship-to-shore cranes from ZPMC were delivered to Tanger Med's Terminal 4 to boost capacity, part of the expansion phase at the APM Terminals-operated facility that TMPA credited for the 8.4% container growth in 2025.

title: CMA CGM and Asyad to build USD 400m multipurpose logistics terminal at Sohar
summary: During Sultan Haitham's state visit to France, CMA CGM and Oman's Asyad Group signed a framework agreement to jointly develop, manage and operate a USD 400m multipurpose logistics terminal at Sohar, giving CMA CGM reliable inland access outside Hormuz as it kept ships inside the Gulf during the Iran conflict. Strengthens Sohar Port & Freezone's position as a Hormuz-bypass gateway competing with Khorfakkan and Fujairah.

title: Sohar added as Gulf call on Gulftainer's new India-Gulf Express service
summary: Gulftainer's weekly India-Gulf Express (GIX) linking Nhava Sheva and Mundra with Sharjah, Sohar, Hamad and Jebel Ali began calling Sohar from October 2025, adding a direct West India connection for Sohar Port ahead of the 2026 surge in Hormuz-bypass demand.

title: Kazakhstan proposes Antwerp-Bruges partnership for Aktau and Kuryk ports on the Middle Corridor
summary: At the Kazakhstan-Belgium Business Council during King Philippe's state visit, President Tokayev proposed a partnership between Port of Antwerp-Bruges and the Caspian ports of Aktau and Kuryk to channel Kazakh metals, petrochemicals and agri-products via the Middle Corridor. Follows a February 2026 pilot shipment of Kazakh rice to Antwerp. Proposal stage; no PoAB response reported.

title: Port of Antwerp-Bruges International signs five-year MoU with Philippine Ports Authority
summary: PoAB International signed a five-year MoU with the Philippine Ports Authority in Manila covering port planning, digitalisation and operational training, as the PPA weighs further terminal investment. Extends PoAB International's advisory footprint into Southeast Asia alongside its India outreach the same month.

title: Port of Antwerp-Bruges joins Belgian PM's Mumbai trade mission to capture post-FTA India cargo
summary: Port of Antwerp-Bruges accompanied Prime Minister Bart De Wever to Mumbai on 4 September 2026 for a high-level trade dialogue aimed at capturing cargo growth following conclusion of the India-EU FTA in early 2026; ports were also placed on the India-BLEU cooperation agenda in October 2026. Positions Antwerp against Rotterdam and Hamburg for India-Europe flows.

title: Misrata Free Zone signs port development MoU with Port of Antwerp-Bruges and Jan De Nul
summary: Libya's Misrata Free Zone signed an MoU with Port of Antwerp-Bruges on 11 June 2026 covering technical and advisory cooperation, capacity building, digital transformation, clean energy, port master planning and development of specialised terminals including a bulk terminal; dredging group Jan De Nul formally joined the partnership. Follows an April 2025 PoAB expert field visit to assess Misrata's equipment and safety.

title: Port of Antwerp-Bruges and ONEX Elefsis sign 'Blue Corridor' strategic partnership
summary: At Posidonia 2026, ONEX Elefsis Port & Logistics Center (Greece) and Port of Antwerp-Bruges signed a strategic partnership to develop port and logistics infrastructure and a trade-and-energy 'Blue Corridor' linking the Aegean and Black Seas with northwest Europe.

title: Antwerp-Bruges, Bremerhaven and Pyeongtaek agree green Ro-Ro corridor
summary: Bremerhaven, Port of Antwerp-Bruges and Korea's Gyeonggi Pyeongtaek Port Corporation agreed to develop a green Ro-Ro shipping corridor between Korea and northern Europe, linking Europe's two largest vehicle-handling ports (Zeebrugge and Bremerhaven) with Korean automotive exports.

title: Port of Duqm, part-owned by Antwerp-Bruges and DEME, hit by Iranian drone strike
summary: Two drones struck the Port of Duqm in Oman on 1 March 2026 injuring one worker, in Iranian retaliation for US/Israeli strikes. Port of Antwerp-Bruges International holds a stake in the Duqm port company alongside DEME through the Consortium Antwerp Port / Port of Duqm Company structure, making it PoAB's main equity exposure in the Gulf region during the 2026 conflict.

title: Port of Antwerp-Bruges International leads Tanzania Ports Authority landlord-model reform workshop
summary: PoAB International NV delivered a strategic workshop in Arusha for Tanzania Ports Authority board members on port governance reform and transition toward a landlord port model. Advisory positioning in a market where DP World (Dar es Salaam berths 0-7) and Adani (CT2) hold the main concessions.

title: Antwerp port experts begin field assessment at Libya's Misrata Free Zone port
summary: A team of Port of Antwerp-Bruges experts began a field visit to the Misrata Free Zone port to evaluate equipment and safety procedures, in preparation for a structured cooperation that led to the June 2026 development MoU with Jan De Nul.

title: ICSID tribunal orders Port of Antwerp-Bruges to pay DP World EUR 41m over Antwerp Gateway expropriation
summary: A split ICSID tribunal ordered Port of Antwerp-Bruges to pay DP World EUR 41m plus costs and interest in the arbitration DP World launched in 2017 against Belgium over partial expropriation of its Antwerp Gateway concession land. Closes a long-running dispute between DP World and the Antwerp port authority.
